title: Ampere Force 3D visualization and experimental teaching platform
summary: Organize DIS screen readings, magnetic field direction identification, and 3D force vectors into the same classroom workflow.
description: For the teaching of Ampere's force experiment and left-hand rule in high school physics, it combines experimental data reading, visual evidence and spatial models to support two complementary entrances for teacher demonstration and student inquiry.
background: Traditional Ampere force teaching tends to stay in the memory of formulas, and experimental readings, magnetic field directions and three-dimensional force relationships are often scattered in different tools. This project attempts to put multiple sources of evidence into the same teaching link.
capabilities: DIS screen capture and ROI digital readout
F1, F2, F3 three force synthesis and three-dimensional display
Research on the spatial relationship between I, B and F on the student side
teachingValue: Transform the left-hand rule from formula memory to evidential reasoning
Help students establish the correspondence between the y-z plane and three-dimensional space
Let teachers present experimental readings, visual evidence, and physical models simultaneously
scenarios: Left Hand Rule Rule Discovery Lesson
Teachers’ open classes and regional teaching and research
technicalHighlights: Color marking and magnetic field direction mapping
roadmap: Continue to verify the stability of OCR under different DIS interfaces
Improve camera space calibration
Form a reusable classroom experiment data protocol

title: FringeLab laser interference and diffraction intelligent analysis platform
summary: Collect laser patterns through cameras, experimental pictures or physical simulations, extract relative light intensity profiles and complete wavelength estimation, model comparison and uncertainty analysis.
description: For single-slit diffraction and double-slit interference experiments, pattern collection, ROI selection, spatial calibration, light intensity profile extraction, feature identification, physical model selection and wavelength estimation are organized into a traceable digital experimental link.
background: Traditional laser interference and diffraction experiments mainly rely on observing bright and dark fringes with the naked eye, manually measuring the spacing and substituting them into formulas. It is difficult to completely present the true light intensity distribution and is not conducive to continuous and repeatable data analysis. FringeLab converts light screen patterns into relative camera response curves, allowing students to move from pattern collection to model inversion and experimental quality evaluation.
imageAlt: FringeLab production interface, the left side displays red laser interference fringes and adjustable ROI, and the right side displays the relative light intensity curve and wavelength measurement results
notice: Camera mode requires HTTPS or localhost, and requires the user to actively grant camera permissions; different phones and browsers have different support for exposure, focus, and white balance lock. Image processing, simulation, curve analysis and session parameter saving are all completed in the current browser, without relying on external analysis backends, and camera frames will not be uploaded. The current version does not provide the manifest and service worker required to install PWA. The source repository is verified but currently private, so the GitHub button does not appear on the public portal.
capabilities: Three inputs: camera, PNG/JPEG/WebP pictures and ideal physical simulation
Strip ROI that can be moved, rotated, and scaled by dragging the corners
Two-point calibration, physical ruler identification and virtual ruler integration
RGB, brightness and automatic channel selection, background subtraction and Gaussian smoothing
Peak, valley, sub-pixel center, FWHM and overexposure plateau detection
Wavelength estimation from multiple dark fringes in single-slit diffraction and multiple bright fringes in double-slit interference
Comparison of exact geometric regression and small angle approximation results
Fresnel number, sampling adequacy, exposure and calibration quality gating
95% expanded uncertainty, ideal model fit, and CSV/JSON/PNG export
Saving and restoring local experimental parameters in the browser
teachingValue: Elevate "looking at stripes" to a quantitative analysis of relative light intensity distribution
Improve formula substitution into model inversion driven by experimental data
Supports experimental quality discussions of saturation, sampling, calibration and uncertainty
Facilitates comparison of theoretical curves, real patterns, exact geometry and small angle approximations
Ideal for classroom demonstrations, student experiments, and research studies
scenarios: Double-slit interference fringe spacing and laser wavelength measurement
Analysis of single-slit diffraction dark fringes and central main maximum width
Comparison of real experimental drawings and ideal models
Discussion on Experimental Error, Uncertainty and Far Field Conditions
Preview of optical simulation experiments without equipment
technicalHighlights: Pure browser pixel processing and real-time curve drawing
roadmap: Continue to verify the differences in exposure and focus control between different mobile phones and cameras
Improve the real ruler homography correction under obvious perspective conditions
Supplement repeated measurement and teaching empirical data under real equipment conditions
For an installable experience, supplement with a proven PWA manifest and offline caching strategy

title: Dual-camera color marker and acoustic field synchronized tracking system
summary: Track an HSV color marker with two cameras, capture microphone features in sync, and analyze the fused data in 2D, 3D, and acoustic-field views.
description: A browser-only tool for combined motion and acoustic-field experiments, bringing dual-camera color-marker tracking, microphone feature extraction, timestamp alignment, and interactive 2D/3D visualization into one workflow.
background: Motion trajectories and sound measurements are often recorded by separate devices, making timing and spatial relationships difficult to compare. This project fuses visual and audio records with a browser monotonic clock and falls back to a single-camera 2D mode when a second camera is unavailable.
notice: Camera and microphone features require HTTPS or localhost and explicit device permission. The displayed dBFS value is relative to digital full scale, not calibrated sound pressure level in dB SPL; dual-camera 3D trajectories also require spatial calibration for the experimental setup.
capabilities: Enumerate, select, and preview two cameras with automatic fallback when the second feed is unavailable
Estimate HSV thresholds from a selected target region and track connected components after morphological cleanup
Extract RMS, dBFS, fundamental frequency, spectral centroid, and zero-crossing rate
Match visual and audio observations by nearest timestamp on the performance.now() monotonic clock
Synchronize 2D trajectories, acoustic-field points, and an interactive rotatable and zoomable 3D trajectory
Export visual, audio, and fused CSV files, a complete JSON session, and PNG trajectory captures
teachingValue: Place kinematic trajectories and acoustic measurements in one traceable experiment workflow
Help students understand time synchronization and fusion across multiple sensors
Support comparison between single-camera 2D recording and dual-camera 3D reconstruction
Provide real data for discussing dBFS, pitch, spectral features, and spatial calibration
scenarios: Synchronized study of moving and sound-producing objects
Investigation of spatial acoustic fields and trajectories
Dual-camera visual measurement and 3D reconstruction lessons
Multimodal experiment data capture and export
technicalHighlights: Vite, TypeScript, and browser-only static deployment
Web Worker image processing and exponential smoothing
Shared monotonic clock with tolerance-based matching
roadmap: Add dual-camera geometric calibration and conversion to physical length units
Establish a dB SPL calibration workflow with fixed gain and a reference sound source
Continue compatibility testing across browsers and multi-camera devices

title: Spot vibration tracking and frequency response experimental system
summary: Use the browser camera to track the red reflected light spot, and automatically associate the displacement range with the driving frequency.
description: Serving forced vibration, periodic vibration and frequency response experiments, real-time spot center of gravity tracking is used instead of frame-by-frame artificial punctuation to form frequency-displacement range data and response curves.
background: Manual video analysis is inefficient, readings are subjective, and frequency and displacement data are easily misaligned. The system combines camera tracking, spatial calibration, frequency sweep recording and chart presentation in the browser.
capabilities: Frequency-displacement range scatter points and curves
teachingValue: Reduce the burden of manual punctuation on a frame-by-frame basis
Help students understand the formation process of frequency response data
Emphasis on term boundaries between peak-to-peak displacement and mechanical amplitude
scenarios: Optical lever or reflected light spot measurement
technicalHighlights: HSV red threshold and weighted center of gravity
roadmap: Add CSV export
Supplementary filtering and outlier processing

title: Demonstration of light intensity and polarization direction of three polarizers
summary: Continuously adjust the three polarization directions P1, P2, and P3 to observe light-intensity projection and Malus's law.
description: A three-dimensional interactive prototype for polarization teaching, explaining the phenomenon of transmitted light reappearing after adding a third polarizer between two orthogonal polarizers.
background: The three-polarizer experiment is often described as counterintuitive. The interactive model unfolds each polarization projection and light intensity attenuation in physical order to help learners build a continuous process model.
capabilities: The angles of the three polarizers can be adjusted independently
Switching between two typical experimental combinations
teachingValue: Connect Malus's law with the continuous projection process
Explain why intermediate polarizers can restore part of the transmitted light
Support teachers to quickly change parameters for comparison
scenarios: Preview before class and review after class
roadmap: Fix web page metadata
Add accessibility keyboard control instructions
